title: The troop train from Baltimore reaches Monocacy

records.says: Arrived here 8.10, moving cautiously with sixteen cars.
records.label: W. P. Smith, "Monocacy, 9.15 P. M., October 17, 1859"

title: When Colonel Lee arrived
reading: Sandy Hook soon after eleven; the marines in the armory yard before midnight
basis: Smith's telegram of that midnight, written where Lee arrived. Greene's times on that night run an hour ahead of every other record.

records.says: At ten o'clock in the evening he came upon a special train from Washington.
Arrived at Sandy Hook before 11, and car with Col. Lee arrived soon after.
records.label: W. P. Smith, "Harper's Ferry, October 18, 1859 ... 12 midnight"

records.says: 11:00 pm Colonel Robert E. Lee and 90 U.S. Marines arrive by train from Washington.
About twelve o'clock, Colonel Lee arrived, having under his command eighty-five marines
records.label: Col. R. W. Baylor

records.says: I did not reach the Ferry until about eleven or twelve o'clock on Monday night
records.label: Lee

records.says: I instantly replied to Mr. Walsh that we had ninety men available

title: When the marines stormed the engine house and took Brown
reading: Stuart at the door at 6:58, the doors broken in at 7:02 and Brown cut down a minute later
basis: Greene's half past six is his order to pick the storming party, before the summons; the papers and the Park Service put the summons at about seven, and Washington was out by half past.

records.says: At half-past six in the morning Colonel Lee gave me orders to select a detail of twelve men for a storming party
At 6:30 AM Lee began the attack
At sunrise, when Lieutenant Stuart gave his signal
Shortly after 7 o'clock, Lieutenant E.B. Stuart … advanced to parley
7:00 am Brown refuses to surrender to Lt. J.E.B. Stuart.
about half-past seven o'clock on Tuesday morning
records.label: Lewis W. Washington, of his delivery

records.says: The whole was over in a few minutes.
the whole fight had not lasted over three minutes.
